description:
Search the user's full conversation history via Postgres full-text search.

CALL search_conversation_history when the user refers to specific past
messages, errors, decisions, or details that you do not already see in
the live context window. Examples of when to call:
 - "What was that error I got on Tuesday?"
 - "What did we decide about stop losses last week?"
 - "Can you check what I said about the Alpaca key?"
 - When the user asks about something specific that was discussed days
   or weeks ago.

Rules:
 - Results are already scoped to the authenticated user (you cannot
   search other users' messages).
 - Results are truncated and capped. Do NOT ask for limit=20 unless
   the default 5 returned nothing relevant.
 - Messages containing secret-shaped strings (API keys, tokens,
   passwords) are silently dropped from results. If the user mentions
   a secret, tell them you cannot surface it from history.
 - This is FACTUAL recall. For user preferences or durable facts, use
   search_memory instead.

conversationId.description: Optional: limit search to a single conversation id. Omit to search across ALL of the user's conversations, which is the usual case.

limit.description: Max messages to return. Defaults to the server-configured maximum (currently 5). Hard ceiling is 20.

query.description: Natural-language keyword search over the user's full message history. Examples: "alpha picks API key error", "TSLA bracket order rejection", "what did we decide about stop losses". The query is passed through Postgres websearch_to_tsquery so plain English works (no boolean operators required).

name: search_conversation_history
title: Search past conversation history
